name: Machine Learning Engineering
tagline: Train, deploy and maintain the models that power predictions, recommendations and AI products.

overview.summary: Machine learning (ML) engineers turn data into models that make predictions — fraud scores, product recommendations, demand forecasts, image recognition, speech and language models — and then put those models into production so they run reliably at scale. The job sits between data science (experimenting with models) and software engineering (shipping robust systems), and increasingly includes MLOps: versioning, monitoring and retraining models over time.
whyTrending: The WEF Future of Jobs Report 2025 lists AI and machine learning specialists among the three fastest-growing jobs to 2030.
Companies that adopted generative AI now need engineers who can fine-tune, evaluate and serve models efficiently, not just call an API.
The US Bureau of Labor Statistics projects computer and information research scientists — the category that includes many ML researchers — to grow 22% from 2025 to 2035.
Cheaper GPUs in the cloud and open-weight models (Llama, Qwen, Gemma, Mistral) let smaller companies train and host their own models, widening demand beyond Big Tech.

roles.title: Machine Learning Engineer
roles.description: Builds training pipelines, trains and tunes models, and deploys them behind APIs or batch jobs.

roles.title: MLOps Engineer
roles.description: Automates the model lifecycle: experiment tracking, model registry, CI/CD for models, monitoring and drift detection.

roles.title: Applied Scientist / Research Engineer
roles.description: Adapts state-of-the-art research to company problems and runs rigorous experiments to prove the gains.

roles.title: Computer Vision Engineer
roles.description: Builds models for images and video — detection, segmentation, OCR, quality inspection.

roles.title: NLP / LLM Engineer
roles.description: Fine-tunes and evaluates language models for classification, extraction, search and generation tasks.

roles.title: Recommendation Systems Engineer
roles.description: Designs ranking and recommendation models for feeds, e-commerce and ads, with online A/B testing.

beginner: Linear algebra, probability and statistics basics
scikit-learn: regression, classification, train/test split, cross-validation
Evaluation metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC, RMSE
intermediate: Deep learning with PyTorch (tensors, autograd, training loops)
Feature engineering and handling imbalanced data
Experiment tracking with MLflow or Weights & Biases
Serving models with FastAPI and Docker
SQL and working with data warehouses
advanced: Model monitoring, data drift and automated retraining
Kubernetes-based ML platforms (Kubeflow, Ray, SageMaker, Vertex AI)

tools: AWS SageMaker / Google Vertex AI / Azure ML
stack.note: PyTorch dominates new postings; TensorFlow still appears in older production stacks. Cloud ML platform experience (SageMaker, Vertex AI or Azure ML) is a frequent 'nice to have'.

roadmap.title: Classic ML foundations
goals: Refresh Python, NumPy, pandas and Matplotlib
Review the maths you need: vectors, matrices, gradients, probability
Train regression and classification models with scikit-learn
Learn cross-validation and choose the right metric for a problem
Enter one beginner Kaggle competition and submit a baseline
roadmap.milestone: A clean notebook that beats a simple baseline on a real dataset, with a clear write-up of metrics.

roadmap.title: Deep learning
goals: Write a PyTorch training loop from scratch
Train a CNN for image classification and a transformer for text
Use transfer learning with a pretrained Hugging Face model
Track experiments with MLflow or Weights & Biases
Learn about overfitting, regularisation and learning-rate schedules
roadmap.milestone: A fine-tuned model published on the Hugging Face Hub with a model card.

roadmap.title: Ship it (MLOps)
goals: Wrap a model in a FastAPI service and containerise it with Docker
Set up CI that runs tests and a quick evaluation on every push
Deploy to a cloud service (Hugging Face Spaces, Render, or a free cloud tier)
Add basic monitoring: latency, error rate and input-drift checks
Write an end-to-end case study with architecture diagram
roadmap.milestone: An end-to-end ML system — data → training → API → monitoring — that an interviewer can try live.

projects.title: House-price or rent predictor
projects.description: Predict Dhaka (or any city) rent prices from listing data; compare linear regression, random forest and gradient boosting.

interview.question: Explain the bias–variance trade-off.
interview.answer: Bias is error from overly simple assumptions (underfitting); variance is error from sensitivity to the training data (overfitting). Increasing model complexity lowers bias but raises variance, so you aim for the balance that minimises validation error.

interview.question: How do you handle an imbalanced dataset?
interview.answer: Use metrics like precision/recall or PR-AUC instead of accuracy, try class weights, resampling (over/under-sampling, SMOTE), adjust the decision threshold, and collect more minority-class data if possible.

interview.question: What is regularisation?
interview.answer: Techniques that discourage overly complex models to reduce overfitting — e.g. L1/L2 penalties, dropout, early stopping and data augmentation.

interview.question: Precision vs recall — when do you prefer each?
interview.answer: Precision matters when false positives are costly (spam filters). Recall matters when missing a positive is costly (fraud, disease screening). F1 balances both.

interview.question: What is data leakage?
interview.answer: When information that would not be available at prediction time sneaks into training — e.g. using future data or target-derived features — leading to great offline scores and poor real-world performance.

interview.question: How does a transformer work at a high level?
interview.answer: It uses self-attention so each token can weigh every other token in the sequence, stacked with feed-forward layers and positional information, enabling parallel training and long-range context.

interview.question: What is transfer learning?
interview.answer: Starting from a model pretrained on a large dataset and fine-tuning it on your smaller task, which saves data and compute and often improves accuracy.

interview.question: How do you monitor a model in production?
interview.answer: Track input data distributions for drift, prediction distributions, latency and errors, and — when labels arrive — real accuracy. Alert on thresholds and trigger retraining or rollback.

interview.question: What is LoRA?
interview.answer: Low-Rank Adaptation freezes the base model and trains small low-rank matrices added to certain layers, making fine-tuning large models far cheaper in memory and storage.

interview.question: Batch vs online inference?
interview.answer: Batch scores many records on a schedule (cheap, high latency, e.g. nightly recommendations). Online serves single requests in real time (low latency, needs scalable APIs, e.g. fraud checks at payment).

demandNotes.bangladesh: Moderate and rising. Fintech (fraud, credit scoring), telecom (churn), e-commerce and offshore R&D teams hire ML engineers; competition is high for few senior seats, so strong portfolios stand out.
demandNotes.remote: High for candidates with deployed models and MLOps skills; pure notebook experience is less valued than shipped systems.
demandNotes.global: Very high. ML specialists are among the WEF's fastest-growing jobs, and research-scientist roles are projected to grow 22% in the US.
